findings.title: Hook exit code semantics
findings.theme: Claude Code hook design (PreToolUse / PostToolUse / Stop / SessionEnd)
findings.key_insight: Exit 2 is the ONLY blocking code. Exit 1 is non-blocking (stderr shown in verbose mode only). Exit 0 is allow (stdout optionally parsed as JSON control). A blocking hook that accidentally exits 1 instead of 2 will silently allow the tool call.
findings.detail: PreToolUse and UserPromptSubmit can block (exit 2). PostToolUse and SessionEnd cannot block — they have already run. Stop hooks can force-continue. Hooks firing on '*' matchers (e.g., log-tool-calls.sh) must never exit 2 or they block every tool call.
findings.recommendation: Any new blocking hook must use `exit 2` with a descriptive stderr message. Distinguish clearly between hard-block (exit 2) and soft-warn (exit 0 + stderr nudge) as done by safety-block.sh vs safety-warn.sh.

findings.title: Anti-rationalization Stop hook (prompt type)
findings.key_insight: The Stop hook uses `type: "prompt"` (not a shell script) — it sends Claude's completed response to a fast model that returns {"ok": false, "reason": "..."} or {"ok": true}. If rejected, Claude must continue. The entire prompt is inline in settings.json under hooks.Stop[0].hooks[0].prompt.
findings.detail: This is a model-calling hook, not a bash hook. Tuning is done by editing the prompt field in settings.json directly. The fast model's JSON response drives the continue/stop decision.
findings.recommendation: Do not conflate prompt-type Stop hooks with bash-type hooks. If adding rationalization checks, keep the prompt tight and the response schema strict ({ok, reason}) to avoid parse failures that silently pass.

findings.title: Hybrid installer: symlinks for content, jq-merge for settings.json
findings.key_insight: Hooks, commands, agents, CLAUDE.md, and statusline are installed as per-file symlinks back into the repo (live-update without reinstall). settings.json is the ONLY file that is merged (not symlinked) because it accumulates per-machine state (enabledPlugins, machine-specific allow/deny rules). The logs/ directory is always a real directory, never a symlink.
findings.detail: Skills get per-directory symlinks (not per-file) and existing non-symlink skill dirs are preserved untouched. install_symlink() checks if the symlink already points to the right source before acting — fully idempotent. --force overwrites foreign symlinks; default backs them up to a timestamped BACKUP_DIR.
findings.recommendation: Do not symlink settings.json — it must be merged to preserve per-machine entries. Do not copy hooks/commands/agents — symlinks allow iterative edits to the repo to take effect without reinstall. Always keep logs/ as a real directory to avoid rotation/rotation scripts failing on symlink targets.

findings.title: jq-merge pattern for settings.json with array dedup and hooks deep-merge
findings.key_insight: Plain `jq -s '.[0] * .[1]'` object-merge loses array entries (last wins). The install.sh merge explicitly reconstructs permissions.deny and permissions.allow as concatenated+unique arrays, and merges hooks with object spread. A .tmp file is written then validated with `python3 -m json.tool` before atomic `mv` — preventing corrupt settings.json on jq failure.
findings.detail: Idempotency guard: if the existing settings.json already references claude-defaults hooks (safety-block.sh, log-tool-calls.sh, etc.) the merge is skipped entirely unless --force is passed. jq absence is handled gracefully: fall back to plain cp with a warning.
findings.recommendation: Never use a plain `jq -s '.[0] * .[1]'` merge for settings.json — it silently drops existing deny/allow array entries. Always reconstruct arrays with `+ | unique`. Always validate the .tmp output before renaming. Always provide a jq-absent fallback path.

findings.title: JSONL tool-call logging with redaction and atomic writes
findings.key_insight: Log writes use a single O_APPEND syscall (via hooks/lib/jsonl-write.py). ENOSPC silently drops the line — logging must never break the tool call. Output is capped at 1 MB with a _truncated_bytes marker. Redaction runs before write via hooks/lib/redact.py covering JWT, AWS, GitHub, Anthropic, OpenAI keys, and common credential flag patterns.
findings.detail: Two row types per call: pre (before tool runs, with args) and post (after, with exit_status, duration_ms, output). A call_id (nanosecond ts + PID) links pre to post. mcp_server is parsed from mcp__<server>__<method> tool names. All write errors are wrapped in `|| true` on the bash side.
findings.recommendation: If extending the logging schema, add new fields to both pre and post schemas consistently. New secret patterns go in hooks/lib/redact.py _PATTERNS plus a case in tests/test-redaction.sh. To backfill redaction on existing logs, use scripts/redact-existing-logs.py (one-off, not auto-run).

findings.title: Bash safety hook pattern design: hard-block vs soft-warn separation
findings.key_insight: Hard-block patterns (safety-block.sh, exit 2) are limited to truly irreversible or catastrophic commands: rm -rf against /, home, or with sudo; dd to raw disk devices; mkfs/wipefs; fdisk partition ops; fork bombs; chmod 777 on /; force-push to protected branches. Everything else is a soft-warn (safety-warn.sh, exit 0 + stderr). This separation prevents alert fatigue.
findings.detail: safety-warn.sh covers sensitive file paths (*.env, *credentials*, *.pem, *.key, id_rsa, etc.) with a stderr nudge only — the Edit/Write still proceeds. Hard deny rules for ~/.ssh/, ~/.aws/, ~/.gnupg/ etc. live in settings.json permissions.deny, not in a hook.
findings.recommendation: Keep the hard-block list narrow and focused on irreversible damage. Sensitive-file warnings belong in safety-warn.sh (soft). Path-level blocks belong in settings.json deny rules. Avoid creeping the hard-block list with recoverable operations.

findings.title: macOS/BSD vs GNU coreutils portability in hook scripts
findings.key_insight: `readlink -f` is GNU-only; macOS/BSD `readlink` does not support `-f`. The SCRIPT_DIR_OF() helper in hooks/lib/common.sh uses a three-tier fallback: (1) greadlink -f if available (Homebrew coreutils), (2) readlink -f if it works (Linux/GNU), (3) portable fallback using `cd` + `pwd` with single-level symlink resolution.
findings.detail: The portable fallback: resolve the symlink one level with `readlink`, then use `cd $(dirname target) && cd $(dirname link) && pwd`. This handles the common case where hooks are symlinked from ~/.claude/hooks/ back to the repo. Relative symlinks are handled by the `case "$link" in /*) ... *)` branch.
findings.recommendation: Never use `readlink -f` bare in hook scripts. Always use the SCRIPT_DIR_OF pattern from hooks/lib/common.sh. Test on macOS without Homebrew coreutils to catch GNU-isms. Similarly, avoid `date -d` (GNU) — use Python or `date -r` / `date -v` for BSD-compatible date arithmetic.

findings.title: Hook stdin parsing pattern with jq null-safety
findings.theme: Claude Code hook design (PreToolUse / PostToolUse / Stop / SessionEnd)
findings.key_insight: Hooks receive their input on stdin as JSON. The extract_jq_field() helper always adds `// "null"` fallback and pipes stderr to /dev/null — preventing unbound variable errors when optional fields (like file_path) are absent. Individual hooks like safety-block.sh use `|| echo ""` fallback on the jq call itself.
findings.detail: Pattern seen across all hooks: `CMD=$(jq -r '.tool_input.command // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")`. The double fallback (jq's `//` operator + bash `|| echo`) ensures the variable is always set even if stdin is not valid JSON or the field is absent.
findings.recommendation: Always use both the jq `//` alternative operator and a bash `|| echo` fallback when reading hook stdin fields. Never assume all fields are present — PreToolUse for Edit will have file_path but not command; PreToolUse for Bash will have command but not file_path.

findings.title: SessionEnd hook for log rotation and pruning
findings.theme: Claude Code hook design (PreToolUse / PostToolUse / Stop / SessionEnd)
findings.key_insight: log-rotate.sh fires on SessionEnd (non-blocking). It gzip-rotates the current day's log if it exceeds CLAUDE_LOG_ROTATE_BYTES (default 100 MB) and prunes logs older than CLAUDE_LOG_RETAIN_DAYS (default 365 days). Both thresholds are overridable via env vars. Rotation uses next-available integer suffix (.jsonl.1.gz, .jsonl.2.gz) — never overwrites an existing rotation.
findings.detail: SessionEnd hooks cannot block. They run after the session closes. This is the correct event for cleanup/rotation tasks that should not delay the user's interaction.
findings.recommendation: Place any session-cleanup tasks (log rotation, temp file cleanup, metrics flush) on SessionEnd, not PostToolUse — PostToolUse fires per-tool and would be far too frequent for rotation checks.

summary: docs/solutions/ does not exist in this repository. All 7 PR themes have direct coverage in existing repo documentation (docs/HOOKS.md, docs/LOGGING.md, scripts/install.sh, hooks/lib/common.sh). The most critical patterns to carry forward: (1) exit 2 vs exit 0 blocking semantics are easy to confuse, (2) jq array merge must use concat+unique not object spread, (3) readlink -f is GNU-only and breaks on stock macOS.
